text:
Anna: Quick sync — we keep hitting ambiguity around shard ownership during bootstart. When a node downloads a safetensors shard, what guarantees do we expect before marking it "SEALED" and using it for inference?
Sam: TL;DR: we need a tiny handshake/lease so two nodes don't both think they own the same shard. otherwise you get competing updates to local caches.
Kevin: Proposal: explicit state machine for a shard on a node: OFFLINE -> FETCHING -> SEALED (read-only) -> ACTIVE (owned, can accept KV writes/evictions decisions) -> EVICTING -> OFFLINE. Transition to ACTIVE requires an ownership lease from control plane or from the previous owner.
Anna: That sounds reasonable. How do we implement the lease cheaply? HTTP call to control plane for canary path?
Kevin: Example handshake (very small):
```
POST /v1/weights/handshake
Headers:
  X-Weight-ID: shard_abc123
  X-Requester: node-34
  X-Generation: 12
  X-Checksum: sha256:aa11bb...
```
Response: 200/409/202 with body (short):
```
{"status":"ACCEPTED","state":"ACTIVE","lease_ms":120000}
```
If 409 -> someone else holds ACTIVE (return SEALED or OFFLINE).
Sam: Important detail: "SEALED" allows reads from the local memory-mapped region but disallows being used as authoritative for shard routing decisions. ACTIVE means you can be chosen for routing and take accounting.
Jen: Tradeoffs: central control-plane leases are simple but add latency on cold fetches. Gossip-based handoff is fast but complex for correctness (split-brain). We could do fast-path optimistic activation: node becomes SEALED immediately, tries to acquire ACTIVE lease async; if clash, reconcile by yielding ACTIVE back to winner.
Anna: Reconciling sounds hairy. Any simpler fallback?
Sam: Simple rule: use checksum+generation to favor higher generation. If equal and both think they can be ACTIVE, last-writer-wins by control-plane oracle. That reduces conflicts post-fact.
Kevin: Also need a short-lived "bootstart proxy" mode: when not fully ACTIVE but needed to serve in-flight requests, node can mark shard as "PROXY_ACTIVE" with strict metrics tagging (degraded latency + limited concurrency) and a short lease (30s). Helps avoid cold failures.
Jen: Metadata propagation: push metadata to local cluster agent + best-effort pubsub to other nodes. Critical transitions (ACTIVE accepted) must be acknowledged by control-plane so routing tables update quickly.
Anna: How about manifests vs manifestless shards? Any different behavior?
Kevin: If we have a manifest, we can precompute generation and checksums so lease decisions are deterministic. Manifestless requires content-hash discovery on fetch — treat generation as 0 until agent registers it. That increases chance of temporary PROXY_ACTIVE.
Sam: Operational note: require that the loader emits an explicit event on transitions. Eg: `loader-bot: shard shard_abc123 -> SEALED @node-34 (checksum sha256:...)` so we can debug.
loader-bot: loader v2 deployed to canary, will emit transition events.
Jen: Quick concern: eviction during handoff. If node goes EVICTING while another is FETCHING, ensure the evicting node serves copies until ACTIVE is granted elsewhere (grace window).
Anna: Ok—action items: 1) Kevin to draft handshake API + state enum (small RFC). 2) Sam to prototype PROXY_ACTIVE mode with metrics. 3) Jen to outline metadata propagation guarantees. 4) Add loader event lines to logging spec.
Sam: +1. I'll do a quick prototype this week. :thumbsup:
Anna: Thanks all. Posting results into the RFC thread once done. :eyes:
